title: County Support Helps Kinship Caregivers Provide Stable Homes
description:
September is National Kinship Care Month, a time to  honor grandparents, aunts, uncles, adult siblings, godparents, stepparents and close family friends who step up to raise children when their parents can’t. In San Diego County, about half of all children in out-of-home care live with kinship caregivers.
 
Kin placements are preferred because they keep children connected to their families, traditions, and culture. But kinship care often begins suddenly, and relatives may not  have the resources to care for a child—especially one with medical or developmental needs.
 
County Child & Family Well Being t provides support and resources that help kinship caregivers create stable, safe homes where children can thrive.
 
For one local grandparent, that support made all the difference. With help from the County, she gained the tools she needed to provide the best possible care for  her granddaughter.
